A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, Spurious Privacy Leakage in Neural Networks. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original membership-inference experiments, group-level privacy measurements, robust-training comparisons, differential-privacy experiments, and architecture evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally displays full group-level ROC curves for FMoW.

M1.justification: The LiRA auditing procedure, ERM/DRO/DFR training methods, DP-SGD experiments, and evaluated architectures remain unchanged. Revised memorization explanations and suggested future poisoning attacks do not introduce an implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Waterbirds, CelebA, FMoW, MultiNLI, CivilComments, and the FMoW16/FMoW4 task variants. The added FMoW plot concerns existing coverage; the medical example and poisoning discussion introduce no evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: ERM/DRO/DFR, online and offline LiRA versus TrajMIA in Table 4, and the architecture comparisons in Section 5. Both versions omit DRO results on FMoW for the same stated reason.

E3.justification: The group-preserving LiRA sampling, evaluation metrics, Waterbirds FPR exceptions, hyperparameter searches, model sizes, and DP settings are retained. Section 5's new statement about a common 0.1% FPR conflicts with unchanged figure axes; it does not establish a protocol change.

E4.justification: The task-complexity, CKA/PCA, memorization, privacy-budget, and DFR L1-versus-L2 analyses already appear in v1 and are retained. The new FMoW ROC figure extends benchmark reporting, while the added architecture discussion interprets existing subgroup plots.

E5.justification: Repeated-run and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged, including five target models in Section 3.2, five seeds for Figure 4, sixteen seeds in Section 5, and the existing mean and standard-error reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds full per-group FMoW ROC curves in Figure 7. v1 already reported the absence of pronounced FMoW privacy disparity and provided selected TPR/AUROC values; the curves supply additional operating-point results. Numerical entries in Tables 1–9 and all retained plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: The ERM, DRO, and LiRA equations and Definitions B.1–B.3 and D.1 remain unchanged. Replacing the group-count notation with |G| and mistakenly referring to existing definitions as theorems do not constitute new mathematical content.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain group privacy disparity, its relationship to task complexity and memorization, robust training's failure to eliminate it, DP utility tradeoffs, and architecture-dependent auditing. The rewritten abstract and conclusion preserve these claims.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly interprets the retained subgroup plots as showing limited mitigation from target-architecture choice. The conclusion develops poisoning and label-free auditing as future directions. However, the added Waterbirds disparity comparison incorrectly describes groups evaluated at different FPR thresholds as a common 0.1% FPR comparison.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the anonymous code-repository link with a named GitHub repository and repeats that access information in the reproducibility paragraph. Implementation settings, hyperparameter tables, hardware, and compute estimates are unchanged; repository contents were not inspected.

R1.justification: The reference entries and substantive positioning relative to privacy, fairness, spurious robustness, and architecture research are unchanged. The conclusion reuses the already-cited Yang et al. (2024) for a future auditing direction rather than adding a new cited work.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, expands introductory motivation with ethical framing and a medical example, and revises the conclusion, removing the separate Impact paragraph while retaining its auditing message. It also adds publication information and local wording edits; most technical exposition and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the FMoW ROC plot as Figure 7, renumbers subsequent figures, revises Table 1 and Figure 4 captions, and repositions retained displays through page reflow. Existing plot graphics and table structures are otherwise preserved.

improvement.justification: The added FMoW ROC curves and clearer motivation modestly improve inspectability and exposition. However, the new Section 5 comparison claims a common 0.1% FPR although Figure 9 evaluates Waterbirds group 2 at 3% and group 3 at 0.1%; the revised conclusion also introduces an unresolved citation. With the core evidence unchanged, these limited benefits and newly introduced accuracy defects do not establish a reliable net quality direction.
